cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Metamorphosis myths involve humans or gods being transformed into animals, plants, stones or constellations

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Ovid's Metamorphoses is the most important literary source — it collects around 250 transformation myths

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Transformations served multiple purposes: punishment, protection, reward, escape and explanation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Daphne was transformed into a laurel tree to escape Apollo's pursuit — Apollo then adopted the laurel as his symbol

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Arachne was turned into a spider after challenging Athena to a weaving contest and winning or matching her

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Narcissus was transformed into a flower after falling in love with his own reflection and wasting away

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Io was turned into a cow by Zeus to hide her from Hera, but Hera claimed the cow and set Argus to guard her

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Actaeon was turned into a stag and torn apart by his own hounds after accidentally seeing Artemis bathing

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Some transformations were merciful — gods sometimes changed humans to protect them from worse fates

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Transformation myths often explained natural features: why the laurel is Apollo's tree, why spiders weave

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: These myths explore themes of power (divine vs mortal), identity, desire and the boundaries between human and nature

cards.front: Recall a key point about Myths of Transformation
cards.back: Ovid's Metamorphoses uses transformation as a metaphor for change, instability and the nature of reality itself
